decisions.why: ICD s10 change process: a daughter that cannot meet it raises a blocking issue against LUM-CAR-A, it does not implement a variant

decisions.what: Common footprint adopted from ICD s7.1: 100.0 x 80.0 mm, R3.0 corners, 5x M3 (4 corners at 5 mm inset + H5 at (46,74)), 1.6 mm FR4, with a mandatory 30x26 mm RJ45 notch at (6,0)-(36,26)
decisions.why: H1-Q4 closed the stack at 11.0 mm; the carrier's board-edge RJ45 is ~15 mm tall so the notch is a hard mechanical stop and the anti-180-degree interlock (ICD s7.4)

decisions.what: Re-baselined onto ICD rev A2 (copied from boards/lumina-carrier/architecture/connector-icd.md)
decisions.why: Two changes bind this board: (1) board-wide HV clearance raised 0.60 -> 0.635 mm per TPS2378 vendor layout guidance, daughters inherit it; (2) new s8.4 - the carrier's TPS16630 load switch has a mandatory 10k SHDN pull-down, so a daughter may assume an unprogrammed/crashed/reset/brownout carrier presents 0 V at J3, not 48 V. Rail limits s6.2 and mechanical s7.1/s7.2 are UNCHANGED.

decisions.what: LED stage stays on +12V (baseline); the P1 '48V is 16x better for dimming slew' argument is WITHDRAWN as an artifact of holding L fixed
decisions.why: Verified algebraically by the orchestrator: with L sized for the same ripple fraction k, t_rise+t_fall = 1/(f*k), independent of Vin. At 700 kHz / k=0.30 both rails give 4.762 us (48V only redistributes 3.81/0.95 us between rise and fall). That is 33.8x the 141 ns PAR-REQ-01 budget, so NO rail or inductor choice reaches the requirement by gating the converter - it needs shunt-FET dimming either way. The 48V branch therefore buys nothing on fidelity and costs 0.635 mm creepage, 100 V caps, bleed path and daughter-owned inrush.

decisions.what: Stackup JLC04161H-3313, 4 layers, 100.0 x 80.0 mm, 1.6 mm
decisions.why: Switch-node containment 11 mm above a live 2.4 GHz antenna (H1-Q8 made Wi-Fi a supported control path), continuous GND reference under jitter-sensitive PWM, B.Cu consumed by two reverse-mounted sockets, ~120 parts in ~45 cm2. No controlled-impedance net exists on this board.

decisions.what: Dimming topology: shunt FET per channel across the LED string
decisions.why: Closes the PAR-REQ-01 TIMING wall: TPS92515HV direct PWM floors at 200 ns vs a 141 ns requirement, but its shunt mode is spec'd 10,000:1 = 10.2 ns min pulse. Implemented T ~ 50-100 ns, 1.4-2.8x margin. The RESOLUTION wall (17 bits needed, LEDC caps at 14) is NOT closable on this board and needs carrier firmware dithering (CR-5).

decisions.what: Design point 150 mA/die, 4 emitter packages, 2S2P per channel; emitters off-board on aluminium MCPCB
decisions.why: Full white = 0.718 A on +12V, 4 % under the sustained ceiling and 2.8x under OCP, so the board is electrically incapable of exceeding its budget with every PWM stuck at 100 %. Off-board MCPCB because 1.6 mm FR4 misses the junction budget by 2-3x. >3 A conditional flag CLOSED (max 0.30 A/channel).

decisions.what: No fifth (amber) channel on rev A; fit BOTH ID mechanisms (ID_ADC bottom-leg divider + I2C EEPROM)
decisions.why: Amber dilutes an af envelope that full white already fills to 96 % of the rail ceiling. ICD s3.3 makes the divider and the EEPROM coexist rather than alternatives - the divider gives board type, the EEPROM per-unit calibration - so PAR-REQ-17 is met without spending a pin.

decisions.what: Q1 CLOSED: enclosure sealed with LED heat conducted through the wall (not vented)
decisions.why: Owner decision: keeps dust out of a basement/garage install over years, and the strobe run independently recommended the same, so both fixtures share one enclosure design. 3.21 W internal -> 38 C air. The wall-conduction path becomes load-bearing for the thermal case and must be written as an explicit testable ENC-x criterion, not an assumption.

decisions.what: Q2 CLOSED: emitter is RGB 3-in-1 + separate white discrete, superseding D3's integrated 4-in-1
decisions.why: Owner decision, taken knowingly against this run's recommendation. Deciding factor: the thermal case now rests on a published 125 C Tj max and 3.5x stock depth rather than on an ASSUMED 12 K/W Rth from a sole-source vendor publishing neither Rth nor Tj max. Retires the 20 K/W marginality risk this run flagged. Consequences owned here: PAR-REQ-15 white/colour fringing becomes the live risk; the entire sustained-power table is stale and must be re-derived; 145 mA/die is reopened.

decisions.what: Q3 CLOSED: PAR-REQ-01 met by hardware + firmware. Strict reading (5% perceived, gamma 2.2) binds.
decisions.why: Carrier firmware commits to PWM-domain dithering >=3-4 bits (CR-5 accepted). Shunt-FET hardware half stands as designed (T ~50-100 ns vs 141 ns). FIRMWARE DEPENDENCY must be named in the design doc so it cannot be silently dropped: without the dither the requirement fails by 4.4-8.9x and no hardware on this board can fix it. Dither must be PWM-domain, not 60 fps frame-domain - a 4.4% dither at 60 Hz breaches IEEE 1789 NOEL on its own.

decisions.what: Q4 CLOSED: same-reel sourcing; 24C32 EEPROM fitted but shipped empty; PAR-REQ-16 and PAR-REQ-17 to be formally amended with original text quoted
decisions.why: No measurement instrument exists today, so colour matching rests on same-reel binning. The EEPROM is fitted so that decision stays reversible. Amending rather than quietly failing PAR-REQ-16 keeps the record honest about what was changed by decision.

decisions.what: PAR-REQ-16 and PAR-REQ-17 formally amended (AMD-01, AMD-02 in requirements.md s0), original text quoted
decisions.why: AMD-01: a chromaticity/flux bin is not an orderable attribute on LCSC/JLC and the selected vendor publishes none, so the BOM line was unbuildable; replaced by single-reel procurement for the whole build. This is a REDUCTION in guarantee, not an equivalent - same-reel is an empirical correlation, a published bin is a contractual limit - so PAR-REQ-06 is carried at reduced confidence with bench verification. AMD-02: hardware (divider + 24C32) is fitted; the calibration DATA is deferred because no colorimeter exists for this build.

decisions.what: The RJ45 notch is the coordinator's to implement via a central board_init --cutout flag. This run does NOT hand-edit Edge.Cuts and does NOT shrink the outline.
decisions.why: Both daughters need the notch, so it is being added centrally rather than worked around per-run. The notch stays a hard keepout in constraints.json meanwhile. Coordinator will confirm the flag exists before this run reaches P5. Supersedes the OPEN-7 remediation (hand Edge.Cuts edit) recorded at H1; the OPEN-7 coordinate-translation trap under fixed-outline board_init still stands and must be re-raised at H2.

decisions.what: P5 outline procedure fixed: board_init --outline 100x80 --corner-radius 3 --mounting-holes 4 --cutout 6,0,30,26, then verify geometry against an expected area of 7212.274 mm2
decisions.why: Coordinator added --cutout centrally (commit 18613d3) so both daughters share it. Expected area derived here so P5 has a number to check rather than eyeballing: 100x80 = 8000, minus the 30x26 notch = 780, minus 4 corners at r=3 = 4 x r^2(1-pi/4) = 7.7257. The outline_origin translation is the trap that would otherwise silently misplace every keepout.

decisions.what: Emitter set: 4x XL-HD6070RGBC-A46L-BD (C22434861) + 4x XL-HD6070UWC-A4-BD (C48586656); 2S2P, 150 mA/die, 300 mA/channel. Headline 0.717 A = 95.6% of the 0.75 A ceiling.
decisions.why: Both live-verified via parts_search this session and spot-checked independently by the orchestrator. The headline survives the package change because BOTH packages publish identical Vf ranges (R 1.8-2.4, G/B/W 2.8-3.4), so the 2S2P/150 mA arrangement falls out the same way - a derived result, not a copy-forward. All nine power rows independently recomputed by the orchestrator and reproduce exactly.

decisions.what: 150 mA/die confirmed over 145 (H1-P7 re-derived, not carried forward)
decisions.why: Every genuine HARDWARE ceiling passes at both: 2.8x on the 2.0 A OCP, 3.4x on the TPS2378 0.85 A MINIMUM limit. The only figure 150 fails is the ICD 8.5 W total, which ICD s6.2 itself calls a firmware-governed average, not a trip. Flips to 145 if the carrier owner declares 8.5 W a hardware limit.

ICD s7.6 internal-air figures are not self-consistent: 69 C (at) vs 56 C (af). Convection is near-linear in dT at this scale, so ~2x the box heat must give ~2x the rise: the ICD own af point (31 K at ~9.9 W) scaled to ~19.2 W gives ~60 K = ~85 C, not 69 C. Independent Hoffman/Rittal calc gives 89-115 C at a 25 C room. Optimistic by 20-46 K. The 56 C af figure survives only at a 25 C room ambient.
